description:
The campaign's working confidence interval: a Wilson score interval over a count out of $N$, validated against an independent computation of its own definition and well-formed at the campaign's largest sample size.

## Background

Every published Monte Carlo estimate in this repository states its sample count and an interval. The only interval implemented in-tree today is a Wilson score interval in a research prototype (`dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/src/stats.rs:38`); the production statistics crate has none. Wilson is the campaign's working interval at large counts, where it is accurate and short; the conservative small-count estimator is separate work behind this leaf on a dependency edge, in the same module.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A Wilson score interval is returned for a count out of $N$ at a caller-supplied level, agreeing to within $10^{-12}$ with an independently computed reference on hand-checked cases including $Z = 0$ and $Z = N$.
- [hard] REQ-02: The estimator returns a well-formed interval at the campaign's largest planned sample size, $N = 2 \times 10^{7}$, with no overflow, no interval of negative width, and no bound outside $[0,1]$.
- [hard] REQ-03: The entry point takes counts, not samples, so it is usable both online against a running accumulator and offline against a published dataset.

## Notes

Scope is the Wilson estimator alone; the Clopper-Pearson estimator, the coverage demonstration, and the which-regime documentation follow in the dependent leaf.
